id: title:CShine612:show alert threshold lines on dashboards after reload

observations.behavior: Adds a new helper function tile_insight_prefetches and its use in dashboard API endpoints.
observations.posthog_connection: This backend change adds database-level prefetching for alert configurations on dashboards. Without this, the frontend receives empty alerts arrays, hiding threshold lines.

observations.behavior: Changes mount-time behavior of insight alerts logic; no longer fetches destination counts immediately when loading dashboards.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces N+1 query risk during dashboard mounting while still hydrating inline alert metadata needed for display.

observations.code_quote: const inlineAlerts = [{ id: 'alert-a', name: 'Inline' }] as AlertType[]
observations.behavior: Adds tests asserting that cached inline alerts are used without triggering additional network requests or list fetching.
observations.posthog_connection: These checks support the reliability improvement by ensuring the UI does not make unnecessary calls when rendering dashboard tiles with pre-fetched alerts.

observations.limitations: All hunks provided are either backend changes, frontend implementation, or unit tests. No production deployment status, adoption metrics, or live incident reports are available. The benefit is inferred from code structure rather than observed runtime performance or user-facing results.

review.reason: The patch demonstrates a substantive and bounded correctness and reliability improvement: it fixes silent loss of alert data in dashboards and prevents an avoidable N+1 request pattern on tile mounts. This is visible across backend prefetching and frontend hydration, but lacks broader systemic reach or critical-path dependency analysis to warrant tier 3.
review.posthog_relevance: This change could help PostHog users who rely on dashboard-based alert threshold lines; missing this would degrade their ability to configure and view those thresholds correctly. It also reduces database load during dashboard loading, benefiting operations and team efficiency.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies solely on supplied diff chunk; no release notes, WPR, or historical context were considered. Tier assignment assumes these hunks represent complete behavior for each component.
